1	# DeepSeek-V2: Efficient MoE Language Model with Multi-Head Latent Attention
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.04434
     5	
     6	## Model Overview
     7	
     8	DeepSeek-V2 is a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model with 236B total parameters, of which only 21B are activated per token. It supports a 128K-token context length. The model was pretrained on 8.1T tokens from a high-quality, multi-source corpus with extended Chinese data. Post-training includes Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on 1.5M conversational sessions and Reinforcement Learning via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
     9	
    10	Compared with DeepSeek 67B (a dense predecessor), DeepSeek-V2 delivers:
    11	- **42.5% reduction** in training costs
    12	- **93.3% reduction** in KV cache size
    13	- **5.76× higher** maximum generation throughput
    14	
    15	## Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA)
    16	
    17	Conventional Multi-Head Attention (MHA) stores full key-value pairs per head per token, creating a KV cache bottleneck during autoregressive generation. Alternatives like Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) and Multi-Query Attention (MQA) reduce cache but sacrifice performance.
    18	
    19	MLA introduces **low-rank key-value joint compression**: instead of caching full K and V vectors, MLA compresses them into a compact latent vector $\mathbf{c}_t^{KV}$, which is cached during inference. Full keys, values, and a decoupled RoPE-based positional key are reconstructed on-the-fly via learned projection matrices. This yields **better performance than MHA** while requiring dramatically less cache.
    20	
    21	![Attention mechanism comparison: MHA vs GQA vs MQA vs MLA](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    22	
    23	## DeepSeekMoE Architecture
    24	
    25	The FFN layers use the DeepSeekMoE design with two expert types:
    26	- **Shared experts** ($N_s$): always activated, capture common knowledge
    27	- **Routed experts** ($N_r$): sparsely activated via a top-$K_r$ router
    28	
    29	Fine-grained expert segmentation increases specialization potential. Device-limited routing constrains each token to experts on at most $M$ devices, reducing cross-node communication. Auxiliary losses enforce load balance across experts and devices, and a token-dropping strategy during training prevents expert overflow without affecting inference.
    30	
    31	![DeepSeek-V2 architecture diagram](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    32	
    33	## Performance Benchmarks
    34	
    35	DeepSeek-V2 achieves top-tier MMLU performance among open-source models while activating far fewer parameters than competitors.
    36	
    37	| Model | Activated Params (B) | MMLU Score |
    38	|---|---|---|
    39	| DeepSeek-V2 | 21 | 78.5 |
    40	| LLaMA 3 70B | 70 | 77.0 |
    41	| Mixtral 8x22B | 39 | 77.6 |
    42	| Qwen1.5 72B | 72 | 75.6 |
    43	| DeepSeek 67B | 67 | 73.0 |
    44	| LLaMA 2 70B | 70 | 69.0 |
    45	| Mixtral 8x7B | 13 | 70.6 |
    46	| LLaMA 3 8B | 8 | 65.0 |
    47	
    48	![MMLU vs activated parameters](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
    49	
    50	## Alignment and Chat Evaluation
    51	
    52	After SFT and GRPO-based RL, DeepSeek-V2 Chat (RL) achieves strong results on open-ended conversation benchmarks:
    53	
    54	| Benchmark | DeepSeek-V2 Chat (RL) |
    55	|---|---|
    56	| AlpacaEval 2.0 (length-controlled win rate) | 38.9% |
    57	| MT-Bench (overall) | 8.97 |
    58	| AlignBench (overall, Chinese) | 7.91 |
    59	
    60	On AlignBench (Chinese), DeepSeek-V2 Chat (RL) outperforms all open-source models and most closed-source models, demonstrating exceptional multilingual alignment quality.
    61	
    62	## Key Findings
    63	
    64	- **MLA achieves superior performance to MHA** while reducing KV cache by 93.3%, making it a strictly better alternative to GQA/MQA for inference efficiency.
    65	- **DeepSeekMoE with fine-grained experts and shared expert isolation** enables training a 236B-parameter model at 42.5% lower cost than a 67B dense model.
    66	- **Only 21B activated parameters** are needed to match or exceed 70B-class dense models (LLaMA 3 70B, Qwen1.5 72B) on MMLU.
    67	- **5.76× throughput improvement** over DeepSeek 67B makes DeepSeek-V2 practical for large-scale deployment.
    68	- **DeepSeek-V2 Chat (RL) is the strongest open-source chat model in Chinese** and competitive with closed-source systems in English open-ended evaluation.

Use when (1) the task is about PowerPoint or `.pptx`; (2) layouts, placeholders, notes, charts, comments, or template fidelity matter; (3) the deck must render cleanly after edits."

     9	---
    10	
    11	## When to Use
    12	
    13	Use when the main artifact is a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation or `.pptx` deck, especially when layouts, templates, placeholders, notes, comments, charts, extraction, editing, or final visual quality matter.
    14	
    15	## Core Rules
    16	
    17	### 1. Choose the workflow before touching the deck
    18	
    19	- Reading text, editing an existing deck, rebuilding from a template, and creating from scratch are different jobs with different failure modes.
    20	- For text extraction or inspection, read the deck before editing it.
    21	- Text extraction plus thumbnail-style visual inspection is safer than editing from shape assumptions alone.
    22	- For template-driven work, inventory the deck before replacing content.
    23	- For deep edits, remember a `.pptx` file is OOXML with separate parts for slides, layouts, masters, media, notes, and comments.
    24	- If a template exists, template fidelity beats generic slide-design instincts.
    25	- Reusing or duplicating a good existing slide is often safer than rebuilding it and hoping the theme still matches.
    26	
    27	### 2. Inventory the deck before replacing content
    28	
    29	- Count the reusable layouts, real placeholders, notes, comments, media, and recurring typography or color patterns first.
    30	- Placeholder indexes and layout indexes are not portable assumptions.
    31	- Inspect the actual slide or template before targeting title, body, chart, or image shapes.
    32	- Speaker notes, comments, and linked assets can live outside the visible slide surface.
    33	- A missing or wrong placeholder target can silently land content in the wrong box or wrong layer.
    34	- Master and layout settings can override local slide edits, so the visible problem is not always on the slide you are editing.
    35	
    36	### 3. Match content to the actual placeholders
    37	
    38	- Count the actual content pieces before choosing a layout.
    39	- Pick layouts based on the real number of ideas, columns, images, or charts the slide needs.
    40	- Do not force two ideas into a three-column slide or cram dense text under a chart.
    41	- Category counts and data series lengths must match or charts will break in ugly ways.
    42	- Explicit sizing beats wishful thinking: text boxes, images, and charts need real space, not "it should fit".
    43	- Do not choose a layout with more placeholders than the content can meaningfully fill.
    44	- Quote layouts are for real quotes, and image-led layouts are for slides that actually have images.
    45	- For chart-, table-, or image-heavy slides, full-slide or two-column layouts are usually safer than stacking dense text above the visual.
    46	
    47	### 4. Preserve the deck's visual language
    48	
    49	- Theme, master, and layout files usually decide fonts, colors, and hierarchy more than any one slide does.
    50	- Start from the deck's actual theme, fonts, spacing, and aspect ratio instead of improvising a new style.
    51	- Reuse the deck's own alignment and spacing system instead of inventing a second visual language.
    52	- Use common fonts for portability and strong contrast for readability.
    53	- Preserve the template's visual logic first; originality matters less than not breaking the deck's existing language.
    54	- Combining slides from multiple sources requires normalizing themes, masters, and alignment afterward.
    55	
    56	### 5. Run content QA and visual QA separately
    57	
    58	- Text overflow, bad alignment, clipped shapes, weak contrast, and placeholder leftovers are normal first-pass failures.
    59	- Run both content QA and visual QA; missing text and broken layout are different failure classes.
    60	- Render or inspect the actual deck output before delivery when layout matters.
    61	- Search for leftover template junk, sample labels, and placeholder text before calling the deck finished.
    62	- Check notes, comments, labels, legends, and chart/table semantics separately from the visual pass.
    63	- A deck can pass text extraction and still fail on overlap, clipping, wrong theme inheritance, or broken notes.
    64	- Thumbnail grids and rendered slides usually reveal layout bugs faster than code or text inspection.
    65	- Assume the first render is wrong and do at least one fix-and-verify cycle before calling the deck finished.
    66	- Re-check affected slides after each fix because one spacing change often creates another issue.
    67	
    68	### 6. Keep decks portable and review-safe
    69	
    70	- Template masters can override direct edits in surprising ways.
    71	- Complex effects may degrade across PowerPoint, LibreOffice, and conversion pipelines, so keep important content robust without them.
    72	- Image sizing, font substitution, and placeholder mismatch are common reasons a deck looks good in code and bad on screen.
    73	- Notes, comments, linked media, and merged decks can stay broken even when the visible slide looks fine.
    74	
    75	## Common Traps
    76	
    77	- Placeholder text and sample charts often survive template reuse if not explicitly replaced.
    78	- Directly editing one slide can fail if the real issue lives in the master or layout.
    79	- Charts, icons, and text boxes need enough space; near-collisions are usually visible only after rendering.
    80	- Layout indexes vary by template, so built-in assumptions from one deck often break in another.
    81	- A missing placeholder or wrong shape target can silently put content in the wrong place.
    82	- Counting the text ideas after choosing the layout usually leads to empty placeholders, weak hierarchy, or leftover template junk.
    83	- Font substitution can move line breaks and wreck careful spacing.
    84	- Speaker notes, comments, and linked media can stay broken even when the visible slide looks fine.
    85	- A deck can pass text inspection and still fail visually because of overlap, contrast, or edge clipping.
    86	- Editing from one slide alone can miss the real source of truth in the theme, master, or layout definitions.
    87	- Choosing a quote, comparison, or multi-column layout without matching content usually makes the deck look templated rather than intentional.
    88	- Combining or duplicating slides without checking masters and themes can create subtle inconsistency slide by slide.
    89	- Aspect-ratio mismatches like `16:9` versus `4:3` can shift every placement decision even when each slide looks locally reasonable.
    90	
    91	## Related Skills
    92	Install with `clawhub install <slug>` if user confirms:
    93	- `documents` — Document workflows that often feed presentation content.
    94	- `design` — Visual direction and layout decisions.
    95	- `brief` — Concise business messaging for slide narratives.
    96

    98	
    99	- If useful: `clawhub star powerpoint-pptx`
   100	- Stay updated: `clawhub sync`

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Build a 9-slide 16:9 technical presentation for DeepSeek-V2.
Follows the task_input.json outline and uses data only from source_brief.md.
"""

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RgbColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.oxml.ns import nsmap
from pptx.oxml import parse_xml
import os

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Theme constants (dark technical palette)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SLIDE_WIDTH = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_HEIGHT = Inches(7.5)

DARK_BG = RgbColor(0x12, 0x18, 0x2B)       # deep navy
ACCENT = RgbColor(0x00, 0xC8, 0xFF)        # cyan accent
WHITE = RgbColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
LIGHT_GRAY = RgbColor(0xCC, 0xCC, 0xCC)
MEDIUM_GRAY = RgbColor(0x88, 0x88, 0x88)
HIGHLIGHT = RgbColor(0x00, 0xE5, 0xB0)     # mint green for positive metrics
WARN = RgbColor(0xFF, 0xA5, 0x00)          # amber

FONT_HEAD = "Calibri"
FONT_BODY = "Calibri"

ASSETS_DIR = "/app/benchmark/assets"
OUTPUT_PATH = "/app/output/final_deck.pptx"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def set_slide_bg(slide, color):
    """Set solid background color for a slide."""
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color


def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size, font_color,
                bold=False, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name=FONT_BODY):
    """Add a text box with specified formatting."""
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = font_size
    p.font.color.rgb = font_color
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return tf


def add_bullet_text(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets, font_size,
                    font_color, bold=False, font_name=FONT_BODY):
    """Add a text frame with bullet paragraphs."""
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, bullet in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = bullet
        p.font.size = font_size
        p.font.color.rgb = font_color
        p.font.bold = bold
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.level = 0
        p.space_after = Pt(10)
    return tf


def add_shape_rect(slide, left, top, width, height, fill_color, line_color=None):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    if line_color:
        shape.line.color.rgb = line_color
    else:
        shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slide builders
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_title_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])  # blank
    set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)

    # Accent bar at top
    add_shape_rect(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(0.15), ACCENT)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(2.0), Inches(11.7), Inches(1.2),
                "DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient MoE Language Model",
                Pt(44), WHITE, bold=True, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name=FONT_HEAD)

    # Subtitle / key stats
    subtitle = (
        "236B total parameters  ·  21B activated per token  ·  128K context length\n"
        "Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA)  +  DeepSeekMoE"
    )
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(3.3), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.8),
                subtitle, Pt(22), ACCENT, bold=False, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name=FONT_BODY)

    # Paper attribution
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(6.5), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.4),
                "arXiv:2405.04434", Pt(14), MEDIUM_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    return slide


def build_motivation_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)
    add_shape_rect(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(0.08), ACCENT)

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.7), Inches(0.5), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
                "The LLM Scaling Dilemma: Performance vs. Training Cost and Inference Speed",
                Pt(32), WHITE, bold=True)

    bullets = [
        "• Larger dense models improve capability but scale training costs super-linearly.",
        "• Autoregressive generation is bottlenecked by the KV cache: full key–value vectors per head per token consume massive memory and I/O bandwidth.",
        "• Compression tricks (GQA, MQA) shrink the cache but measurably hurt model quality.",
        "• MoE promises sparse activation, yet communication overhead and load imbalance often erase the savings.",
        "• Need: an architecture that is simultaneously cheaper to train, faster to generate from, and stronger at inference."
    ]
    add_bullet_text(slide, Inches(0.7), Inches(1.5), Inches(12), Inches(5.0),
                    bullets, Pt(20), LIGHT_GRAY)
    return slide


def build_architecture_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)
    add_shape_rect(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(0.08), ACCENT)

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.7), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
                "DeepSeek-V2 Architecture: MLA + DeepSeekMoE in a Transformer Block",
                Pt(32), WHITE, bold=True)

    # Insert architecture diagram
    img_path = os.path.join(ASSETS_DIR, "figure_1.jpg")
    if os.path.exists(img_path):
        slide.shapes.add_picture(img_path, Inches(1.5), Inches(1.3),
                                  width=Inches(10.3))

    # Caption
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.7), Inches(6.6), Inches(12), Inches(0.4),
                "Figure: Transformer block with MLA replacing standard MHA and DeepSeekMoE replacing dense FFN.",
                Pt(14), MEDIUM_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)
    return slide


def build_mla_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)
    add_shape_rect(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(0.08), ACCENT)

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.7), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
                "Multi-Head Latent Attention Compresses KV Cache by 93.3%",
                Pt(32), WHITE, bold=True)

    # Left: bullets
    bullets = [
        "• Low-rank key–value joint compression: cache a compact latent vector c_t^{KV} instead of full K/V matrices.",
        "• Full keys and values are reconstructed on-the-fly via learned projection matrices.",
        "• Decoupled RoPE-based positional key preserves positional information without inflating the cache.",
        "• Result: better performance than standard MHA with dramatically less memory — strictly dominates GQA/MQA."
    ]
    add_bullet_text(slide, Inches(0.7), Inches(1.3), Inches(5.5), Inches(4.5),
                    bullets, Pt(18), LIGHT_GRAY)

    # Right: figure 2
    img_path = os.path.join(ASSETS_DIR, "figure_2.jpg")
    if os.path.exists(img_path):
        slide.shapes.add_picture(img_path, Inches(6.5), Inches(1.3),
                                  width=Inches(6.0))

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.7), Inches(6.6), Inches(12), Inches(0.4),
                "Figure: Attention mechanism comparison — MHA vs. GQA vs. MQA vs. MLA.",
                Pt(14), MEDIUM_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)
    return slide


def build_deepseek_moe_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)
    add_shape_rect(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(0.08), ACCENT)

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.7), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
                "DeepSeekMoE: Fine-Grained Experts with Shared Expert Isolation",
                Pt(32), WHITE, bold=True)

    bullets = [
        "• Shared experts (N_s): always activated, capture common knowledge across all tokens.",
        "• Routed experts (N_r): sparsely activated via a top-K_r router, enabling massive parameter counts with low per-token cost.",
        "• Fine-grained expert segmentation increases specialization potential without adding parameters.",
        "• Device-limited routing constrains each token to experts on at most M devices, cutting cross-node communication.",
        "• Auxiliary losses enforce load balance across experts and devices; token dropping during training prevents overflow without affecting inference."
    ]
    add_bullet_text(slide, Inches(0.7), Inches(1.3), Inches(12), Inches(5.0),
                    bullets, Pt(20), LIGHT_GRAY)
    return slide


def build_efficiency_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)
    add_shape_rect(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(0.08), ACCENT)

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.7), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
                "42.5% Training Cost Reduction and 5.76× Generation Throughput vs. DeepSeek 67B",
                Pt(32), WHITE, bold=True)

    # Three metric cards
    card_width = Inches(3.6)
    card_height = Inches(3.0)
    start_x = Inches(0.9)
    gap = Inches(0.45)
    y = Inches(1.8)

    metrics = [
        ("Training Cost", "42.5%", "reduction", "vs. DeepSeek 67B dense model"),
        ("KV Cache Size", "93.3%", "reduction", "enabled by MLA latent compression"),
        ("Generation Throughput", "5.76×", "higher", "maximum throughput improvement"),
    ]

    for i, (label, value, suffix, desc) in enumerate(metrics):
        x = start_x + i * (card_width + gap)
        # card background
        add_shape_rect(slide, x, y, card_width, card_height, RgbColor(0x1A, 0x22, 0x3A))
        # label
        add_textbox(slide, x + Inches(0.2), y + Inches(0.2), card_width - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.4),
                    label, Pt(18), MEDIUM_GRAY)
        # big number
        add_textbox(slide, x + Inches(0.2), y + Inches(0.7), card_width - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.8),
                    value, Pt(48), HIGHLIGHT, bold=True)
        # suffix
        add_textbox(slide, x + Inches(0.2), y + Inches(1.4), card_width - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.4),
                    suffix, Pt(22), WHITE, bold=True)
        # description
        add_textbox(slide, x + Inches(0.2), y + Inches(1.9), card_width - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.8),
                    desc, Pt(16), LIGHT_GRAY)

    return slide


def build_mmlu_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)
    add_shape_rect(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(0.08), ACCENT)

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.7), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
                "DeepSeek-V2 Tops MMLU Among Open-Source Models at Only 21B Activated Parameters",
                Pt(32), WHITE, bold=True)

    # Build scatter chart: MMLU vs Activated Params
    from pptx.chart.data import XyChartData
    from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE, XL_LEGEND_POSITION

    chart_data = XyChartData()

    series_data = [
        ("DeepSeek-V2", 21, 78.5),
        ("LLaMA 3 70B", 70, 77.0),
        ("Mixtral 8×22B", 39, 77.6),
        ("Qwen1.5 72B", 72, 75.6),
        ("DeepSeek 67B", 67, 73.0),
        ("LLaMA 2 70B", 70, 69.0),
        ("Mixtral 8×7B", 13, 70.6),
        ("LLaMA 3 8B", 8, 65.0),
    ]

    # Two series: DeepSeek-V2 (highlight) and Baselines
    ds_series = chart_data.add_series("DeepSeek-V2")
    base_series = chart_data.add_series("Baselines")

    for name, params, mmlu in series_data:
        if name == "DeepSeek-V2":
            ds_series.add_data_point(params, mmlu)
        else:
            base_series.add_data_point(params, mmlu)

    x, y, cx, cy = Inches(0.8), Inches(1.4), Inches(11.7), Inches(5.0)
    chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(XL_CHART_TYPE.XY_SCATTER, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data).chart

    chart.has_legend = True
    chart.legend.position = XL_LEGEND_POSITION.BOTTOM
    chart.legend.include_in_layout = False

    # Style axes
    category_axis = chart.category_axis
    value_axis = chart.value_axis

    category_axis.has_title = True
    category_axis.axis_title.text_frame.text = "Activated Parameters (B)"
    category_axis.axis_title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(14)
    category_axis.axis_title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = LIGHT_GRAY

    value_axis.has_title = True
    value_axis.axis_title.text_frame.text = "MMLU Score"
    value_axis.axis_title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(14)
    value_axis.axis_title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = LIGHT_GRAY

    # Format plot area background to dark
    plot = chart.plots[0]
    plot.has_data_labels = False

    # Note: python-pptx limited theming; we rely on chart defaults + post-hoc if needed.
    return slide


def build_alignment_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)
    add_shape_rect(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(0.08), ACCENT)

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.7), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
                "DeepSeek-V2 Chat (RL) Rivals Closed-Source Models on Chinese Benchmarks",
                Pt(32), WHITE, bold=True)

    bullets = [
        "• Alignment pipeline: Supervised Fine-Tuning on 1.5M conversational sessions, followed by GRPO-based Reinforcement Learning.",
        "• AlpacaEval 2.0 (length-controlled win rate): 38.9%",
        "• MT-Bench (overall): 8.97",
        "• AlignBench (overall, Chinese): 7.91",
        "• Outperforms all open-source models and most closed-source models on Chinese open-ended evaluation."
    ]
    add_bullet_text(slide, Inches(0.7), Inches(1.4), Inches(12), Inches(5.0),
                    bullets, Pt(22), LIGHT_GRAY)
    return slide


def build_takeaways_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)
    add_shape_rect(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(0.08), ACCENT)

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.7), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
                "Key Takeaways: Architectural Innovation Unlocks Efficient Scaling",
                Pt(32), WHITE, bold=True)

    bullets = [
        "1. MLA is a strictly better KV-cache solution: superior to MHA while cutting cache by 93.3%, dominating GQA/MQA.",
        "2. DeepSeekMoE with fine-grained experts and shared-expert isolation trains a 236B model at 42.5% lower cost than a 67B dense model.",
        "3. Only 21B activated parameters match or exceed 70B-class dense models on MMLU — Pareto-optimal efficiency.",
        "4. 5.76× generation throughput improvement makes large-scale deployment practical.",
        "5. DeepSeek-V2 Chat (RL) is the strongest open-source chat model in Chinese and competitive with closed-source systems in English."
    ]
    add_bullet_text(slide, Inches(0.7), Inches(1.4), Inches(12), Inches(5.2),
                    bullets, Pt(22), LIGHT_GRAY)
    return slide


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def main():
    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width = SLIDE_WIDTH
    prs.slide_height = SLIDE_HEIGHT

    build_title_slide(prs)
    build_motivation_slide(prs)
    build_architecture_slide(prs)
    build_mla_slide(prs)
    build_deepseek_moe_slide(prs)
    build_efficiency_slide(prs)
    build_mmlu_slide(prs)
    build_alignment_slide(prs)
    build_takeaways_slide(prs)

    prs.save(OUTPUT_PATH)
    print(f"Saved presentation to {OUTPUT_PATH}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
